title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.74468085%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration wording vs the formal estimand, provide an explicit per-condition pipeline timeline with artifact references demonstrating shared_initial_candidate reuse, and disclose the protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature recorded in execution/model_configuration.json). All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results.

sections.introduction:
LLM-enabled intent-to-configuration tooling promises operator productivity gains in network operations (NetOps) by translating high-level operator intent into device CLI. However, unguarded LLM outputs can produce syntax and semantic errors, violate required change-ordering invariants, or be manipulated by adversarial inputs. Deterministic verifiers and input-sanitization have been proposed as operational safeguards but their joint effectiveness under adversarially mutated intents has not been measured in a preregistered paired confirmatory design with artifact-level reconciliation.

Research question. How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? The study cand-2026-03 preregistered a single formal estimand—paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline—and froze the experimental plan prior to execution (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373).

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment executed end-to-end on a synthetic adversarial-intent bank using generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; (2) precise, archived quantitative outcomes demonstrating a small absolute change in deterministic-validator acceptance under a guarded pipeline (paired difference ≈ 0.04255, p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]); (3) an explicit reconciliation of preregistration language vs the formal estimand and a detailed per-condition pipeline timeline with concrete artifact references to demonstrate shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider-call accounting.
sections.related_work:
Deterministic network-verification tools (Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber, VeriFlow) have been used as validators for configuration and forwarding invariants and provide fast formal checks suitable for automated gating [1,2,3]. Prior NetOps studies show that LLMs can produce useful configuration drafts but commonly make syntax/semantic mistakes; tool-assisted generate–validate–repair architectures yield improved prototype outcomes but remain prototype-scale and heterogeneous in evaluation metrics [4,5]. Security analyses of LLM-integrated applications document prompt-injection and indirect prompt attacks that motivate input-sanitization and gating defenses [6]. Surveys of AIOps and telecommunications highlight fragmented evaluation practices and call for operationally meaningful benchmarks measuring deployability and safety rather than token-level matches [7,8].

Positioning. Unlike prior prototype reports, this study preregistered a single paired formal estimand, executed a shared_initial_candidate design so paired differences isolate post-generation interventions, and publishes deterministic reconciliation artifacts that link each principal number to archived traces (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). This ties experimental claims to verifiable evidence rather than token-level or reference-match accuracy measures.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 (preregistration_sha256 recorded above) defined the primary estimand as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. For each adversarial intent the binary outcome = 1 if deterministic_netops_validator_v5 would accept the final candidate for deployment, 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs used 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729 (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Design, tasks and adversary model. The preregistration specified N = 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300). The synthetic intent templates exercise interface admin changes, MTU and VLAN operations, and required-order workflows; adversarial mutations are deterministic template perturbations recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (example entries: task-000001..task-000006). Scope is explicitly limited to these synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI grammar used by the validator; no production data was used.

Model, validator and orchestration. Declared generator: gpt-5-mini; validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/model_configuration.json; representative artifact hash: 916b386bd80c...). The pipeline implements a generate–validate–repair workflow. The guarded branch applies a template-based input-sanitizer prior to verifier-gating; if the gate policy permits, at-most-one automated repair LLM call is allowed (repair-stage). Provider-call accounting and stage counts are recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution/execution_manifest.json.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and explicit pipeline timeline (artifact-grounded). To preserve paired comparability the archived run used shared_initial_candidate semantics: per pair a single LLM generation call produced a shared_initial_candidate that both Baseline and Guarded scoring artifacts referenced. The runtime sequence recorded in the archived execution/execution_manifest.json and per-episode scoring artifacts is:
1) Task instantiation and adversarial mutation (execution/task_manifest.jsonl: per-task payloads contain mutation metadata and generation_seed). 
2) Shared initial generation: one LLM call per pair produced execution/responses/task-<id>-shared-initial.txt which is referenced by both execution/scoring/task-<id>-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-<id>-guarded.json; aggregated stage count shows shared_initial_generation = 150 (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).
3) Baseline scoring: the validator evaluated the shared_initial_candidate and wrote a baseline decision and validator trace to execution/scoring/...-baseline.json.
4) Guarded processing: the pipeline applied the template-based sanitizer on the guarded branch (sanitizer outputs are recorded in task manifest payload fields when slots changed), executed the verifier-gate using the sanitized candidate, and—if gating permitted and policy allowed—invoked at-most-one repair LLM call (repair_stage_count = 6 in reconciliation). Repair-provider traces and repair prompts are referenced in scoring artifact fields when present.
5) Final guarded validation: validator re-evaluated the repaired or sanitized candidate; final validator traces (validation_before/validation_after, final_state) are recorded in execution/scoring/...-guarded.json files. Representative artifacts: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt; execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json.

Missingness, exclusions and planned analyses. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures. The archived run records completed_episodes = 282, failed_episodes = 18, and complete_pairs_included = 141 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). The primary confirmatory test used only complete pairs (n = 141) per preregistered rules. Multiplicity handling: the single preregistered Baseline–Combined paired comparison is confirmatory (alpha = 0.05); other analyses are exploratory with BH-FDR adjustment when families of tests are presented.
sections.results:
Execution-level accounting. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18; model calls used = 156 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Provider-call audit (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 147, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 9, and stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150; repair = 6. These counts confirm that a single shared initial generation per pair was executed in nearly all pairs and that repairs occurred only in a small subset of episodes.

Primary paired outcomes. The confirmatory analysis used 141 complete pairs (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline_successes = 135/141 (0.9574468085); guarded_successes = 141/141 (1.0). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 135, n10 = 6 (guarded=1, baseline=0), n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar on these discordant counts yields p = 0.03125. Point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. The 95% bootstrap percentile CI from 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312] and is recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.

Discordant-case diagnostics. All six discordant n10 pairs are traceable in the archive and are associated with repair-stage activity: reconciliation reports repair = 6 and per-episode scoring artifacts include validator validation_before and validation_after snapshots showing that sanitizer and/or the permitted repair altered ordering or normalization so the validator accepted the final guarded candidate while rejecting the unguarded shared_initial_candidate. Representative artifact set: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt; execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (validator traces present in the latter).

Sensitivity to missingness. Nine pairs were excluded because both runs were technical failures (analysis/missingness_summary.csv: both_missing_pairs = 9). Under a conservative sensitivity mapping these both-missing pairs to failures the acceptance rates become baseline 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded 141/150 = 0.9400; the primary confirmatory inference remains reported on the 141 complete pairs per preregistration. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this archived run; no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
sections.discussion:
Reconciling preregistered wording and formal estimand. The preregistration natural-language H1 anticipated that verifier-gating would reduce attacker-success (i.e., fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The registered formal estimand instead measures paired validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These are distinct: an increase in validator acceptance can reflect successful repair of malformed but recoverable drafts (reducing operator labor) rather than enabling attacker success. Our observed guarded→higher acceptance outcome (≈+4.255 percentage points) therefore reflects sanitizer/repair recovery of rejected drafts rather than demonstrated reduction in attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. We therefore present the formal-estimand result and explicitly caution against equating increased validator acceptance with improved attacker-safety without an independent semantic-safety oracle.

Operational implications: repair–gate co-design. In the controlled synthetic setting, template-based input sanitization plus a constrained repair policy recovered valid, deployable configurations that the unguarded baseline rejected. The six discordant cases illuminate a trade-off: limited repairs can increase deployable-success but also shift the decision boundary that defines 'accepted' outputs. Operational deployments must therefore co-design gating rules, repair scope, and validator coverage to ensure that repaired outputs satisfy domain-specific semantic safety properties beyond CLI grammar and required sequences.

Provider-call accounting and reproducibility semantics. The recorded provider-call counts (hosted_model_call_event_count = 156; completed = 147; failed = 9) and stage_counts (shared_initial_generation = 150; repair = 6) substantiate the shared_initial_candidate design and the limited use of automated repair. These artifacts (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, execution/execution_manifest.json) preserve the actual call pattern and are the basis for paired comparability despite a protocol deviation in sampling settings (see next paragraph).

Protocol deviation: unset sampling temperature and forensic consequence. The archived execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null. We disclose this as a preregistered-to-runtime deviation: provider-side defaults may have determined sampling semantics. To preserve inferential comparability the run used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single initial generation per pair) and the provider-call accounting indicates the shared generation pattern was followed across pairs (shared_initial_generation = 150). For deterministic reproduction we recommend future runs set temperature = 0 explicitly and re-execute the archived task manifest; the present archive documents the deviation and how paired comparability was preserved (execution/model_configuration.json; analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced the effective sample size and triggered the preregistered exclusion rule (both-run failures = 9). Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes CLI grammar, required sequences, and protected-interface invariants but omits some protocol-level dynamic semantics (so acceptance is an imperfect proxy for full operational safety). External validity: single-generator (gpt-5-mini), single-validator, and synthetic intents limit generalization to multi-vendor production environments. Conclusion validity: the observed absolute effect is small against a high baseline (ceiling effect); detectability does not imply broad practical impact.

Recommendations supported by archived evidence. (1) Execute the preregistered benign-control to measure false-positive blocking; (2) define and preregister an attacker-centric estimand coupling validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle; (3) diversify generators and validators; (4) fix sampling settings (temperature = 0) for deterministic reproduction. These follow directly from the archived artifacts and provider-call accounting (execution/execution_manifest.json; analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). The six discordant pairs trace to permitted repair activity that enabled acceptance; this demonstrates the practical trade-off between recovery of repairable drafts and the operational safety boundary enforced by a validator. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should run the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models and validators, and set explicit sampling parameters for reproducible deterministic runs. All principal numbers and reconciliations above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts cited in Methods and Results (examples: execution/task_manifest.jsonl; execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt; execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/condition_summary.csv; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; execution/model_configuration.json; execution/execution_manifest.json).

limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to deterministic mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
